The evidence from Q2 2026 segment performance data shows mid-market and enterprise segments outperform SMB/startup segments across several key metrics:

- **Lower monthly logo churn**: SMB churn is 4.8%, while Mid-market is 2.1% and Enterprise is 1.3% [NL-012#NL-012-S03], [NL-016#NL-016-S03], [NL-015#NL-015-S03], [NL-001#NL-001-S04], [NL-023#NL-023-S03].
- **Higher customer satisfaction (NPS)**: SMB has an NPS of 31, versus 47 for Mid-market and 52 for Enterprise [NL-012#NL-012-S03], [NL-015#NL-015-S03], [NL-016#NL-016-S03], [NL-001#NL-001-S04], [NL-023#NL-023-S03].
- **Higher expansion revenue**: SMB generated $18,000 in expansion revenue in Q2, while Mid-market generated $64,000 and Enterprise generated $91,000. Enterprise alone represents 52.6% of the total $173,000 expansion revenue [NL-012#NL-012-S03], [NL-012#NL-012-S05], [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
- **Disproportionate revenue share**: Mid-market and enterprise customers combined generate 83.8% of recurring revenue [NL-016#NL-016-S03].
- **Superior unit economics**: Enterprise has an LTV:CAC ratio of 16.0x ($350,000 LTV / $22,000 CAC), compared to SMB's 8.3x ($25,000 LTV / $3,000 CAC) [NL-016#NL-016-S03].
- **Higher net revenue retention (NRR)**: Enterprise and mid-market accounts are credited with keeping overall NRR at 116%, while SMB accounts are described as volatile with weak long-term retention [NL-015#NL-015-S03], [NL-023#NL-023-S03].

In aggregate, this data confirms that mid-market and enterprise segments are more stable, more profitable, and more satisfied, whereas the SMB segment shows high churn and low expansion potential [NL-012#NL-012-S03], [NL-016#NL-016-S03], [NL-001#NL-001-S04], [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
